value.first: Week 1: Six months is a good window to start, once he can sit with support and hold his head steady - which lines up right with where he is now. Pick one calm meal a day, when he's happy and not starving. Offer a few spoonfuls of something smooth: iron-rich meat, lentils, or a single-grain cereal, or a soft strip of food he can hold. Keep milk feeds exactly as they are - food is a bonus, not a replacement yet.
value.second: Weeks 2-3: Build to two meals a day and widen the menu - one new food every couple of days so you can spot any reaction. Include the common allergens early and often: smooth peanut, egg, dairy, well-cooked. Expect most of it to end up on his chin, and expect gagging that looks alarming but is him learning to move food back. Loud gag, going quiet, or blue lips is choking - that's different.
value.third: By week 4: Three meals is a reasonable rhythm, with more texture - mashed and soft lumps rather than fully smooth. You'll know it's working when he opens for the spoon, reaches for food, and slowly takes more. Some days he eats little; that's normal at this age. If he's consistently refusing all food, not gaining, or you see swelling or a rash after a food, worth raising with your doctor.
